newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No easy way out to markets for "early" Caspian oil.
newsitem.headline: No easy way out to markets for "early" Caspian oil.

text.p: Russian and Chechen oil firms have a web of political, financial and legal differences to untangle before "early" oil from a major new Caspian oil venture can reach world markets, industry officials said on Tuesday.

While Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Aslan Maskhadov, head of Russia's rebel region Chechnya, talked politics in the Kremlin on Monday, key oil transportation negotiations involving the two sides are continuing on a commercial level.

Politics are bound to bear on the outcome of discussions on the transport of oil, key to both sides' economies, particularly Chechnya's. But the oil talks have complications of their own which could affect oil exports pencilled in for late this year.
"I would say that a final oil transport deal is a long way from being ready," said a senior source at Russia's oil pipeline monopoly Transneft, who wished to remain anonymous.
"Of course we are watching what happens on a presidential level, but there are also economic problems -- both legal and financial -- which need to be solved," he added.
Transneft owns a pipeline which runs from Baku in Azerbaijan to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet of Novorossiisk, crossing the independence-minded republic of Chechnya.

The Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC), an $8 billion international consortium developing major Caspian oil fields off the Azeri coast, plans to use the so-called northern route to export early oil by the end of this year.
Renovating the damaged route would take around a month once a final transport deal had been struck, said Emir Gantamirov, Moscow representative for YUNKO, Chechnya's oil company.
This leaves around three months for the two sides to reach a final deal, if AIOC is to meet its targets. The biggest hurdle to that agreement is the thorny issue of tariffs.

Transneft has proposed giving Chechnya $1.65 per tonne of oil transported through the 160 km (100 mile) Chechen stretch of the 1,500 km (940 mile) pipeline. YUNKO asked for $2.09, although Gantamirov said proposed tariffs could change.
He said he was optimistic the hurdle could be cleared.
"I think Transneft will eventually agree to our proposed increases, as it would not lose money if it did."
Gantamirov added that the two companies may hold official talks later this month, but the Transneft source was cautious.
"There probably will not be any official talks (in August)," he said. "We are maintaining contact on a working group level, and have given YUNKO a plan for an agreement."
An oil transport deal is vital to Chechnya's economy in the near term. The region was ravaged by a bitter 21-month war with Russia which ended with a shaky peace deal last August.

The oil pipeline survived relatively unscathed and would cost only $2.3 million to repair. But major investment is needed to renovate other oil facilities, not least the old and battered Grozny refinery.
AIOC said it was still hopeful an export agreement could be reached in time for it to deliver its first crude oil to world markets by the end of this year.
"We will need that pipeline before the end of this year," said Tamam Bayatly, an AIOC spokeswoman in Baku.
Bayatly said Transneft had a deal with Azeri state oil firm SOCAR, which is also part of the AIOC consortium, to transport its oil along the route by October 1.
"We have to believe in what Transneft has undertaken with SOCAR, and that is to be ready by October 1," Bayatly said.
The Russia-Chechnya oil transport deal is key to AIOC, as the only other existing export route, from Baku to Georgia's Black Sea coast, is not due to be ready until late 1998.
AIOC, led by a British Petroleum -Statoil alliance, plans 1998 output of 1.5 million tonnes (30,000 barrels per day), rising to 700,000-800,000 bpd by 2007-2010.
Its main output would have to travel along a new pipeline, but the route has yet to be chosen and must wind its way through a maze of geopolitical forces at large in the Caucasus region.
